meta.title: Semiconductor Dependency Map
meta.disclaimer: Informational, not investment advice. I am not a financial or tax advisor. Prices are point-in-time and may be stale; verify before acting.

diversified.label: Diversified brand
diversified.detail: Chips are one input of many

adjacent.label: Adjacent
adjacent.detail: Related but off the strict fabrication chain

tiers.label: End product / brand / hyperscaler
tiers.detail: decides what device or compute to build

callout.title: Who pays for all of this
callout.body: Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta and Oracle are projected to spend about $700–745B combined on capex in 2026, roughly 75% of it AI-infrastructure related. Google's TPU and Amazon's Trainium blur the line between brand and chip designer. OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI drive major demand but are private, so they are not shown as nodes.

tiers.label: Chip designers
tiers.detail: create the IP / blueprint for each component

tiers.label: Foundries
tiers.detail: the only three that can manufacture sub-7nm chips

tiers.label: Critical inputs
tiers.detail: the raw dependencies no designer or brand can work around

callout.title: Why the funnel narrows here
callout.body: Every leading-edge chip, whoever designs or sells it, passes through the same few machines and materials. Only ASML makes EUV lithography machines, and Ajinomoto's ABF film insulates almost every advanced chip package. A brand can switch designers and a designer can switch foundries, but nobody can route around this layer.

nodes.name: Apple
nodes.role: Designs its own silicon and assembles the device

nodes.name: Samsung
nodes.role: Designs its own silicon and is also a foundry (same company as the Tier 3 entry)

nodes.name: Amazon (AWS)
nodes.role: Buys Nvidia GPUs; also designs Trainium (via Marvell)

nodes.name: Microsoft (Azure)
nodes.role: Azure earns over $100B a year; heavy Nvidia and OpenAI buyer

nodes.name: Google (Cloud)
nodes.role: Buys Nvidia GPUs; also designs TPU (via Broadcom)

nodes.name: Meta
nodes.role: By some counts the largest single buyer of Nvidia GPUs; also MTIA custom chips

nodes.name: Oracle
nodes.role: OCI plus "Stargate": a $300B, 5-year infrastructure deal with OpenAI

nodes.name: CoreWeave
nodes.role: Buys Nvidia GPUs wholesale and rents them to OpenAI, Microsoft and Meta

nodes.name: Qualcomm
nodes.role: Snapdragon mobile SoC design

nodes.name: AMD
nodes.role: Ryzen CPUs and GPUs

nodes.name: Nvidia
nodes.role: GPUs and AI accelerators

nodes.name: Intel (design arm)
nodes.role: Core CPU design

nodes.name: Micron
nodes.role: Memory (RAM) design

nodes.name: TSMC
nodes.role: Leading-edge manufacturer; most designs land here

nodes.name: Samsung Foundry
nodes.role: Manufactures for others and for itself

nodes.name: Intel Foundry
nodes.role: Newest entrant; developing 18A / RibbonFET

nodes.name: ASML
nodes.role: Sole maker of EUV lithography machines, designed and built in-house

nodes.name: Applied Materials
nodes.role: Deposition, etch, ion implantation, polishing; competes with Lam Research and Tokyo Electron

nodes.name: Canon
nodes.role: Nanoimprint lithography: stamps patterns instead of projecting them; ~90% less power, unproven for logic

nodes.name: Ajinomoto
nodes.role: Makes ABF, the near-100% monopoly insulation film for chip packaging

nodes.name: Viavi Solutions
nodes.role: Tests the interconnects and optics between chips; off the fab chain, a different chokepoint

nodes.name: imec
nodes.role: Belgian research institute in Leuven: neutral pre-competitive R&D shared by ASML, TSMC, Intel, Samsung and Applied Materials. A 30+ year ASML partner, with a joint High-NA EUV pilot line and €2.5B of EU Chips Act funding. Not investable.
